faq:
How much does a new seawall cost in South Florida?

Most residential seawalls run $450–$1,200 per linear foot depending on water depth, wall height, and access. A typical 100-ft residential replacement often lands between $60,000 and $120,000 all-in, with deep-water or high-exposure sites pushing higher.

Do I need permits to build or replace a seawall?

Yes. Nearly all seawall work in South Florida requires permits from your city/county plus Florida DEP and often the Army Corps of Engineers. Replacements in the same footprint are usually faster to permit than new walls or extensions, which can trigger environmental review and mitigation for seagrass or mangroves.

How long does a seawall last, and when should it be replaced?

A well-built modern concrete or vinyl seawall lasts 40–60 years in Florida's marine environment. Warning signs it's time to replace include cracking or leaning panels, soil washout or sinkholes behind the cap, rusting rebar, and separated joints — repairs can extend life, but severe failure calls for full replacement.

High-end$150,000–$400,000+ per projectMulti-slip custom design, elevator/floating dock systems, dual lifts, IPE decking, fish stations, full electrical, smart controls

Where the investment goes: Labor & installation 40–55% · Materials 30–45% · Engineering, permits & mgmt 10–20%.
cost_drivers: Permitting is the single biggest wildcard in South Florida — FDEP, Army Corps of Engineers, county, and municipal approvals can add months and thousands in fees, especially near seagrass, mangroves, or manatee zones. Water depth, tidal conditions, and distance from shore dictate piling counts and barge/marine equipment needs, while Florida's hurricane wind and wave-load codes require heavier engineering and helical or jetted pilings. faq:
Do I need a permit to build a dock in South Florida?

Yes. Most docks require permits from FDEP, the Army Corps of Engineers, and your county or city, plus possible HOA approval. Environmental reviews for seagrass, mangroves, or manatee habitat can extend timelines to 3–9 months, which is why permitting and engineering are built into every quote.

How much does a boat lift add to my dock cost?

A quality boat lift typically adds $12,000–$40,000+ depending on capacity. A standard 10,000–16,000 lb four-post lift runs $12,000–$25,000 installed, while larger elevator or beamless lifts for yachts and heavier vessels can exceed $40,000.

What is the best decking material for a Florida dock?

Pressure-treated pine is the most affordable but requires more maintenance, composite (Trex-style) offers low upkeep and good longevity for a mid-range budget, and IPE or concrete deliver premium durability against sun, salt, and storms. Composite is the most popular choice for balancing cost and low maintenance in our humid marine environment.

title: Seawall Repair
scope: Crack and spall repair, cap rebuilds, tieback and anchor restoration, soil grouting for washouts/sinkholes behind the wall, and drainage correction.
trades: Diagnostic inspection, structural concrete repair, tieback restoration, and pressure grouting under one schedule.
brands: Polyurethane grouts, epoxy injection, galvanized/aluminum tiebacks
cost_table:
TierInvestment RangeWhat's Included
Standard$150–$350 per linear ftCrack sealing, spalling patch repair, minor cap restoration, tieback inspection
Premium$350–$700 per linear ftStructural crack injection, new anchors/deadmen, void grouting, riprap toe protection, drainage weep holes
High-end$700–$1,500+ per linear ftFull cap replacement, panel/king pile reinforcement, vinyl or concrete facing overlay, engineered storm upgrades

Where the investment goes: Labor & installation 40–55% · Materials 30–45% · Engineering, permits & mgmt 10–20%.
cost_drivers: South Florida seawall repair cost is driven heavily by water access and staging — barge-based or waterside work runs far higher than land-accessible sites. Permitting through DEP, Army Corps, and local municipalities (plus environmental/manatee windows) adds time and engineering fees, while salt-water corrosion, tidal exposure, and current storm-load codes push material and structural specs. Failing tiebacks, undermined footings, and soil washout behind the wall are the biggest hidden cost multipliers.
faq:
Can I repair my seawall or does it need full replacement?

If the panels and king piles are structurally sound and damage is limited to cracks, spalling, or a failed cap, repair (roughly $150–$700/linear ft) is usually viable. Once you see bowing, sinkholes behind the wall, or widespread rebar corrosion, replacement often becomes the smarter long-term investment.

Do I need a permit to repair a seawall in South Florida?

Most structural repairs require permits from your local municipality and often DEP or Army Corps approval, especially anything below the waterline or that expands the footprint. Cosmetic patching above the tide line is sometimes exempt, but we always verify before starting to avoid stop-work orders and fines.

What's the most common cause of seawall failure here?

Soil erosion and washout behind the wall — driven by tidal action, heavy rain, and failing weep holes or tiebacks. This creates voids and sinkholes near the cap. Catching it early with grouting and drainage repair costs a fraction of what a collapsed wall replacement runs.

brands: Composite decking, boat-lift cables/motors, marine hardware
cost_table:
TierInvestment RangeWhat's Included
Standard$1,500–$6,000 per projectMinor repairs: decking board replacement, loose piling bracing, hardware/bolt swaps, lift cable and motor service
Premium$6,000–$20,000 per projectPiling replacement, stringer and frame repair, full decking re-lam, lift gearbox/motor rebuild and re-cabling
High-end$20,000–$60,000+ per projectStructural rebuild, multiple pilings, new lift install, seawall-tie repairs, permitted storm-hardened upgrades

Where the investment goes: Labor & installation 40–55% · Materials 30–45% · Engineering, permits & mgmt 10–20%.
cost_drivers: Water access is the biggest cost swing — barge, floating platform, or diver crews cost far more than land-side work, and marine-grade materials (galvanized/stainless hardware, marine pilings, aluminum lift components) carry a premium in salt-water environments. Permitting through the Army Corps, Florida DEP, and local municipalities can add weeks and cost, especially if repairs touch pilings, seawalls, or expand the existing footprint. Storm-code engineering, tidal conditions, marine growth, and hidden underwater rot often push final costs above the initial estimate.
faq:
Do I need a permit to repair my dock in South Florida?

Like-for-like repairs (replacing decking or existing pilings in the same footprint) often qualify as maintenance and may not need a permit, but any structural change, footprint expansion, or seawall/piling work typically requires permits from your municipality, Florida DEP, and sometimes the Army Corps. We confirm requirements before starting to keep the project compliant.

How much does boat lift repair usually cost?

Cable and hardware replacement typically runs $800–$2,500, motor or gearbox service $1,500–$4,000, and a full lift rebuild or new lift install can reach $8,000–$20,000+ depending on capacity and lift type. Saltwater corrosion is the main driver, so we recommend annual servicing to avoid larger failures.

How do I know if my dock needs repair or full replacement?

If pilings are rotted or leaning, stringers are cracked, or more than 30–40% of the structure is compromised, replacement is usually more cost-effective than piecemeal repairs. We provide an inspection, including underwater piling assessment, and give you an honest recommendation with cost comparisons for both options.

faq:
How much does a luxury kitchen remodel cost in South Florida?

Most luxury kitchen remodels run $75,000 to $250,000, with high-end custom projects exceeding $500,000 depending on cabinetry, stone, appliances, and structural work.

Do I need permits for a kitchen remodel in Miami or Fort Lauderdale?

Yes—any plumbing, electrical, gas, or wall changes require permits, and condo/HOA approval is common in waterfront buildings. Cosmetic-only swaps may not, but we recommend permitting for resale and insurance protection.

Why are luxury kitchens more expensive in high-rise condos?

Elevator-only material access, association work-hour rules, sound/water-proofing requirements, and rerouting plumbing within concrete slabs all add labor and coordination costs that single-family homes don't face.

cost_drivers: In South Florida, luxury bathroom cost is driven mostly by finish level and skilled labor — natural stone slabs, waterproofing to code, and specialty trades (glass, tile setters, plumbers) command premium rates in coastal markets like Miami, Fort Lauderdale, and Palm Beach. High-rise condo projects add cost via HOA approvals, elevator/loading logistics, restricted work hours, and stricter plumbing/waterproofing requirements above occupied units. faq:
Why do luxury bathroom remodels cost more in South Florida condos?

High-rise and coastal condos add costs through HOA review, insurance/COI requirements, freight elevator scheduling, limited work hours, and stringent waterproofing since any leak affects units below. These logistical constraints can add 15–30% versus a comparable single-family home remodel.

Do I need a permit for a luxury bathroom remodel?

Yes. Any project touching plumbing, electrical, or structural elements requires permits in Miami-Dade, Broward, and Palm Beach counties. Moving walls, relocating fixtures, or adding steam showers triggers additional inspections; expect permitting and management to run roughly 10–15% of the total budget.

What single upgrade adds the most cost?

Natural stone — especially book-matched marble slabs and full-height stone walls — is the biggest cost driver, followed by structural reconfiguration and steam/spa systems. Material alone can double a mid-tier budget, and stone fabrication and setting require premium specialty labor.
